classification.habitat: Dry plains, saline or sandy soils, scrub and open sites
classification.distribution: Northwestern and northern parts of the Indian subcontinent; exact range varies by source

identification.description: Aromatic branched undershrub with narrow lanceolate leaves and small composite flower heads.
identification.whole_plant: Perennial aromatic shrub/undershrub with several branches.
identification.root: Woody root system; root is a commonly cited useful part.
identification.stem: Erect, branched, becoming woody toward the base; young portions may be hairy.
identification.leaf: Simple, alternate, lanceolate to oblanceolate leaves, usually grey-green and aromatic when crushed.
identification.flower: Small composite heads arranged in clusters, generally pinkish to purplish.
identification.fruit: Small cypsela typical of Asteraceae, usually associated with a pappus.
identification.seed: Small dry cypsela with pappus hairs aiding dispersal.
identification.bark: Older basal stem becomes woody; bark is not the principal crude drug.
identification_points: Root is a commonly used part

therapeutics.precautions: Botanical identity should be checked carefully because Rasna is a name associated with more than one plant in traditional sources.

major_constituents: Sesquiterpenes and other volatile constituents have been reported
phytochemistry.chemical_notes: Chemical composition depends on plant part, geography and extraction; use pharmacognostic literature for exact markers.

modern_information.evidence_summary: Pluchea lanceolata has been investigated in experimental studies related to inflammation and pain. The available evidence does not justify presenting it here as a proven treatment for arthritis or other diseases.
modern_information.safety_notes: Correct botanical identity is particularly important because the name Rasna can refer to different taxa in traditional literature.

viva_questions: Why is botanical authentication important for Rasna?
mnemonics: Rasna = remember root + aromatic Asteraceae shrub.
student.quick_revision: Rasna (Pluchea lanceolata): aromatic Asteraceae undershrub; root is commonly used; botanical authentication is important because Rasna is a disputed/variable traditional name.

teaching_points: Demonstrate aromatic leaves and composite inflorescence.
Discuss the problem of vernacular/classical name-to-species mapping.
discussion_points: Traditional Vatahara profile versus modern evidence
practical_points: Observe leaf shape, indumentum and odour.
Inspect Asteraceae flower head and pappus-bearing cypsela.

doctor.quick_reference: Rasna is traditionally used in Vata- and Shotha-related contexts; confirm the botanical identity before therapeutic selection.
key_precautions: Do not infer dose from this page
